summary: No reachable vulnerabilities. --styles (src/playtest/cli.ts): only accepted with --replay-code and --lineup (STYLES_ONLY_ERROR in both run and replay-without-lineup paths); value split on ',' and each slug checked with Object.hasOwn against a fixed 4-entry map, so prototype keys (__proto__, constructor, toString) and empty entries are rejected; count must equal size-1 where size is already bounded 2..10; duplicate --styles rejected by the existing parser; errors are fixed strings (no echo of input). Randomness: replacement style uses Xoshiro128(fnv1a32(`${code}/${seat}/replace`)) with nextIntUnbiased; no Math.random anywhere in src. In the app the code comes from crypto.getRandomValues and the draw happens in nextHand after the hand is finished, so the user cannot steer it; in the CLI the user-supplied --replay-code only affects a local dev tool. Style choice is a training-variety decision, not money fairness, so a seeded PRNG is appropriate (spec §8). Hidden information: the replay code is read only in nextHand (main thread) after the hand ends and is nulled for the next hand; the new bot decides through the unchanged playerView/botDecisionSeed path, so it learns nothing extra. Names (Jay..Zed) are generic original first names. nextBotName: nextReplacementName loops at most ~11 times (at most 10 seated names), increments by one per replacement, and replacementName throws RangeError only past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, which is unreachable in any session; numbered suffixes keep names unique. No new dependencies, secrets, file or network operations.
